answer:
Canada's defence policy, Strong, Secure, Engaged [C1, C3, C7], and the DND/CAF Data Strategy [C1, C3, C7] describe a desired end state [C1, C2] in which data is leveraged to provide increased efficiency and an information advantage in military operations and corporate applications. [C1, C2] Achieving this end state will require assistance from AI and other automated decision systems. [C1, C2] Defence priority areas [C1, C2] such as NORAD modernization, National Defence Operations and Intelligence Centre (NDOIC), and Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (JISR) [C1, C2] envisage the incorporation of AI and related technologies in the development of a modernized Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) spine. [C1, C2]

The DND/CAF AI Strategy commits the Defence Team to becoming AI-enabled by 2030 [C4, C6], in line with its goals for an overall digital transformation by that date. [C4, C6] Becoming AI-enabled also offers the opportunity to meet the call for modernization and reconstitution. [C4, C6] AI will be foundational to defence modernization. [C5, C8] The fusion of AI, networking, predictive and prescriptive analytics, ML, and robotics will be critical to equip DND/CAF and digitally transform defence. [C5, C8] This will provide the capabilities needed to ensure operational superiority over adversaries and technological parity and interoperability with allies. [C5, C8] To reach its AI goals, DND/CAF needs an AI Centre of its own. [C10, C9] The Centre would serve as a hub of AI expertise for the Defence Team. [C10, C9] It would identify and support the integration of capabilities developed by industry, academia, or allies. [C10, C9]

content_blocks.text:
Canada's defence policy, Strong, Secure, Engaged, and the DND/CAF Data Strategy describe a desired end state in which data is leveraged to provide increased efficiency and an information advantage in military operations and corporate applications. Achieving this end state will require assistance from AI and other automated decision systems. Defence priority areas such as NORAD modernization, National Defence Operations and Intelligence Centre (NDOIC), and Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (JISR) envisage the incorporation of AI and related technologies in the development of a modernized Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) spine.

The DND/CAF AI Strategy commits the Defence Team to becoming AI-enabled by 2030, in line with its goals for an overall digital transformation by that date. Becoming AI-enabled also offers the opportunity to meet the call for modernization and reconstitution. AI will be foundational to defence modernization. The fusion of AI, networking, predictive and prescriptive analytics, ML, and robotics will be critical to equip DND/CAF and digitally transform defence. This will provide the capabilities needed to ensure operational superiority over adversaries and technological parity and interoperability with allies. To reach its AI goals, DND/CAF needs an AI Centre of its own. The Centre would serve as a hub of AI expertise for the Defence Team. It would identify and support the integration of capabilities developed by industry, academia, or allies.
